newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle fall limit on liquidation, rumor.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle fall limit on liquidation, rumor.

text.p: Long liquidation sparked by further commercial pressure and a rumor that an Indiana rose farmer may have died from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, a human version of so-called "mad cow" Disease, touched off sell stops in CME live cattle and April fell as much as the daily limit of 1.5000 cents near midsession, traders said.
At 1125 CDT, April live cattle was down the 1.500 cent limit at 68.800 cents with other months down 1.400 to 0.350 cents. June was down 1.400 at 64.400 cents.
The scientific name of mad cow disease is bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
Live cattle were already pressured by expectations of topping soon in cash markets when the BSE talk surfaced, traders said.

Cattle were pressured by further commercial selling prompted by expectations that cash markets are near a top and the next move may be lower, especially with the Cattle-on-Feed report Friday expected to show heavy numbers of cattle on feed. Increased fed cattle supplies are expected going into the summer and seasonal demand for beef will be easing in the next couple of weeks after retailer booking for the Father's Day and Memorial Day weekend subside, they said.
Cash beef had been strong the past week with boxed beef values up to five-week highs.

Estimates for the number of cattle on feed in large feedlots in the seven primary states averaged 107.6 percent of a year ago and ranged from 106 to 108 percent. Placements averaged 103.3 percent and ranged from 100.5 to 107 percent and marketings averaged 100.6 percent and ranged from 98 to 104.5 percent.

Feeder cattle futures fell along with live cattle as carryover pressure touched off sell stops. Feeders had been supported by lower corn futures early, but the break in live cattle sparked general selling interest, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.17 at $70.65 per cwt.
At 1137 CDT, feeder cattle were 1.000 to 0.100 lower with May off most at 70.650 cents.
